newsitem.title: USA: States urge FTC to tighten pay-per-call services.
newsitem.headline: States urge FTC to tighten pay-per-call services.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal said Monday that 29 U.S. states were urging the U.S. Federal Trade Commission to toughen regulations of pay-per-call services.
The attorneys general want the commission to require disclosure of pay-per-call charges when advertisements solicit calls to a pay-per-call number, including international numbers.
Disclosure should also be required if calls to an 800 number refer a consumer to a pay-per-call service number, Blumenthal said.
He said consumer complaints over the practices were on the rise in Connecticut and other states.
"Too often, consumers are opening their phone bills and finding exorbitant charges for calls they never knew were being charged as a pay-per-call service," Blumenthal said.

He said that while most consumers knew that calls to 900 numbers would incur charges, many were unaware that pay-per-call services had expanded to international numbers, toll-free numbers and other avenues.
